Text:
If I could have given zero stars I would have. After 3 1/2 months ownership, both the freezer and the refrigerator have stopped working. But that's the least of my problems. The real trouble began when I called Samsung for warranty servicing. Summary: 6 days, 6 phone calls, 3 failed promises of a call-back, 1 cancelled appointment, I finally have an appointment for a service tech. to come out and see what the problem might be - IN TWO DAYS! The tech. was very candid when he told me that Samsung would send out the part in 24 hours BUT because they don't ship on weekends I can expect to wait an additional 4 days for them to return to install the part. Best case scenario: my family of 6 will be without a refrigerator for 10 DAYS! Samsung has got to do a better job responding to warranty requests. They have to start offering servicing on weekends. They have to offer a far better call-back response time than they're promised "24-48 hours" (4-8 hours should be expected). And THEY HAVE TO FOLLOW THROUGH ON THEIR PROMISE TO CALL BACK. Oh, and the have to offer a better service schedule than 6 days!

SAMSUNG, BACK UP YOUR PRODUCTS WITH REASONABLE SERVICE!

Summary: Poor quality and poor customer service
Text: I bought this refrigerator 2 years ago. First, do not put anything of any weight on the refrigerator door. I put a gallon of milk on it, and the shelf broke. After making many aggravating calls to Samsung, we received the correct replacement 6 months later after receiving 3 incorrect shelves and being told repeatedly they were the right shelves. They weren't even a close match - 2 were shaped differently and one was an inside shelf, not a door shelf at all. Second, you must have both ice makers on at the same time. It is impossible to turn just one off. Also, the bottom ice maker stopped working for a few months and then out of the blue started working again. The top ice maker constantly gets jammed and freezes over. The outside water/ice dispenser drips after filling your glass and if not wiped up winds up on your floor or dripping down the stainless steel finish. Ugh!! I also had a problem with a Samsung microwave within one year of use. Customer service was a nightmare. I would never buy another Samsung appliance again.

So far so good! I must have spent HOURS reading reviews on refrigerators before settling on this one. Seems they all ALL have one issues or another. I think a lot of it just comes down to personal preference, which is hard to know until you own it. We were upgrading from an older GE profile side-by-side SS fridge that suddenly died (while we were on vacation of course). After several trips to Home Depot and Lowes testing out different designs, this fit the bill when it came to size, look, design, and price. It also had a lot more reviews on the HD and Lowe's websites, with most being positive. I decided to purchase it through the seller on Amazon since it was about $500 cheaper than Home Depot or Lowe's Memorial Day appliance sale price. I knew I was taking a risk with delivery, but took a chance thinking "hey, we've moved fridges before". Overall the delivery process was smooth. I didn't receive notification from the shipping company right away, so called and from then on they were ON IT and gave me updates almost daily. The shipping info did say it would only be delivered curb side in certain states, but CA was not on there so was hoping they'd bring it all the way in. Turns out it was too wide for our front door, and removing door hinges etc is against their policy, so it was left in the garage. Not going to lie, getting it into the house was a bit of a nightmare and the only reason I may consider spending more next time and having HD or Lowes deliver (assuming they bring it in no matter what obstacles). Had to take the front door off the door hinges, remove a patio light, and even with 2 big guys and a commercial dolly, it leaned against our outside brick wall and dented a small area.The dent is small, but seeing it is a constant reminder for my husband so we will be purchasing a new left door (fyi, no magnets will stick to the area to cover it). Replacement left door is $200 on Sears parts, so even with a new door, the fridge was still cheaper than HD or Lowes.

Not going to list all the pros because they're covered in other reviews. I will say the showcase door though is fabulous for households with kids. I stick their drinks and snacks in there for easy access and they don't have to call me every 5 sec saying they can't find something (heaven forbid it's not right in front of their face and they have to move something over...same goes for the husband). Also, we have friends/family over frequently and this is a good place to put water/beer/soda etc so people aren't rifling through your fridge judging your food purchases :) I was also worried about fingerprints since our last SS fridge was hard to keep clean and stainless steel cleaners only streaked and made it look worse. Happy to report that smudges and fingerprints clean up beautifully on this one with Weimans SS cleaner. Looks as good as new (aside from the dent...grrr) after that.

Some cons are: 1) the water/ice maker dispenser sits at an angle to where it's easy for water/ice to overshoot the cup 2) condiment space on the left door isn't the best with the ice maker taking up room, but I've still been able to fill it up with smaller condiment bottles 3) no egg storage, but really, is it that big of a deal to keep them in the carton? Sure it looks nicer, but it always seemed liked unnecessary work moving them from the carton to a plastic tray. If it's that important, sure you could buy an egg storage tray on Amazon for a few bucks.

Overall we are totally happy with our new fridge.

This review is for model # RF323TEDBSR, a stainless steel, French door unit purchased in 2012 for just over $3,000.  Samsung phones and electronics are fine but their refrigerators are awful.  For the first 4 years we had no problems with this refrigerator although some poor design choices became apparent immediately like the shallow refrigerator-wide drawer that can only be pulled out if you open BOTH refrigerator doors; the two fruit and veggie drawers that are constructed in a way that allows crumbs and bits of food to become trapped between the clear plastic drawer walls and are impossible to reach and clean; the shiny facing on the exterior water dispenser that began chipping and falling off.  Then, in 2016, the ice maker stopped working and we cannot get the ice maker door opened to find out why; ice also builds up on the back wall of the refrigerator and must be chipped off.  This ice now creates pools of water in the fruit and veggie drawer and finally, the freezer drawer became impossible to open due to the suction of the seals and caused the handle to break off.  We had to place a 1/8" felt pad on the seal to reduce the suction on the door.  Overall, we will never purchase any Samsung kitchen appliance again.  They've been making refrigerators since 1974 and selling them in the U.S. since the early 2000's so they have had plenty of time to de-bug their products.  Stay away from Samsung refrigerators.

Summary: Save the user manual and start a log of repairs - Good Bye Samsung
Text:
Loved this refrigerator until it was delivered, then we had repair person after repair person at our house over 5 months. They ripped out the icemaker and installed another one, then the door handle on the refrigerator came loose. The icemaker started leaking again and the repairman caulked it! The kids were afraid to get water out of the door because you never knew when it would spray you in the face (if you were under 3 feet tall). The freezer constantly had frost all over the food. After almost $3k for this refrigerator, we didn't want to give up, but it finally gave up after 4 years, when it stopped refrigerating. Good bye Samsung - welcome Frigidaire (no more wet faces or clothing when getting water).
BTW, every time I called Samsung, the representative was on the fringe of rudeness - really!
